nodes.label: CLI as a thin front-end
nodes.rationale: Each command resolves settings, calls a single function in analysis/ or models/, and renders the dataclass it gets back. Nothing in the CLI decides anything a library caller could not also decide - this split is what makes a second front-end (HTTP API) additive rather than a rewrite.

nodes.label: Global CLI options (--verbose/--debug/--format/--quiet)
nodes.rationale: Options belong to the application rather than a command, so they precede the command name. --format json implies --quiet so that piping into jq works without stripping ANSI escapes.

nodes.label: CLI exit-code taxonomy (0/1/2)
nodes.rationale: 1 means PyQuant ran and the data or bundle was wrong; 2 means the command line itself was wrong. The distinction matters in scripts. Failure paths assert non-zero exits rather than only success - the gap that PYQ-120 was.

nodes.label: pyquant train command
nodes.rationale: Reported metrics come from the best checkpoint, not the live post-fit model, because early stopping means the final epoch's weights are usually not the ones being scored (invariant 11).

nodes.label: Named dataset pin (TTL-exempt panel snapshot)
nodes.rationale: Pins are exempt from the cache TTL, which is what makes an experiment replayable months later - one of the three legs of reproducibility alongside the seed and the recorded code version. cache prune never touches pins; that is the entire point of a pin being a separate concept from a cache entry.

nodes.label: Pooling is not a free win (measured worse)
nodes.rationale: On an AAPL+ARM comparison (investigations.md#pyq-315) the pooled model scored worse than training each symbol alone. One comparison, one pair - directional, not settled - but enough that the README no longer states pooling's benefit as a rationale.

nodes.label: pyquant backtest command (walk-forward)
nodes.rationale: Each origin trains up to its own cutoff and scores the window starting at cutoff+1; consecutive origins evaluate disjoint windows. A five-window backtest is 25 predictions with an effective sample size around 5 because overlapping horizons are not independent draws - which is why the docs carry a +36.2% result without promoting it over the 280-prediction headline.

nodes.label: Per-trade round-trip cost in basis points
nodes.rationale: Default 5.0 bps applied to signal P&L: a signal that is only profitable at zero cost is not a signal.

nodes.label: pyquant tune command (Optuna search)
nodes.rationale: Every trial selects on the same data, so the winner is retrained and scored on a held-out period no trial ever saw; that number is reported rather than the in-search validation loss, which is optimistically biased by construction. Default 5 epochs per trial - trials are meant to be cheap and comparative, not converged.

nodes.label: pyquant forecast command
nodes.rationale: Every predicted step is strictly beyond the last observed bar, and the dates in the table, JSON, PNG and appended rows are one set (invariants 3, 4, 14). Non-monotonic bands are reordered for display and the count reported as n_quantile_crossings rather than hidden.

nodes.label: Options snapshot is display-only, never a model input
nodes.rationale: The options snapshot is printed as live market context when use_options is on but is never fed to the model.

nodes.label: pyquant explain command
nodes.rationale: Prints a caveat when the bundle's recorded skill is non-positive: attributing importance within a model that does not beat persistence tells you what the model leaned on, not what moves the price. Permutation importance and the TFT's variable-selection weights agree only on the top feature (Spearman rho ~ 0.3) - investigations.md#pyq-314.

nodes.label: pyquant scan command
nodes.rationale: One symbol failing does not sink the run: untrained comes back as not_trained and failing as error, each as its own row. The signal classifier and row shape are shared with the HTTP API's POST /scan so the two front-ends cannot drift apart.

nodes.label: pyquant snapshot command (options history accrual)
nodes.rationale: yfinance exposes only a current option chain, never history, so running this on a schedule is the only way the project can ever build a historical options-implied series (OptionsPutCallRatio, OptionsATMIV, OptionsIVSkew).

nodes.label: pyquant doctor command
nodes.rationale: Exits non-zero if any bundle's feature schema can no longer be satisfied, turning a broken bundle into something you find by asking rather than by a forecast failing three weeks later. Key presence is reported; key values never are.

nodes.label: pyquant cache list/prune/rm-pin
nodes.rationale: A cached panel is never replayed across a feature redefinition: the cache key fingerprints the feature set, so a redefinition misses rather than serving a stale panel under a new meaning (invariant 15).

nodes.label: CLI --format json output contract
nodes.rationale: Every serializer lives in pyquant.analysis.serialize - the same module the HTTP API builds its responses from, so a CLI document and an API response come from one implementation rather than two schemas that happen to agree today. Fields requiring configuration are omitted rather than raising.

nodes.label: Forecast dates are shipped, never re-derived
nodes.rationale: A consumer should not have to rebuild an exchange calendar - holidays included - to find out which day a prediction is for.

nodes.label: Every rate carries its denominator (invariant 12)
nodes.rationale: evaluation_to_dict emits each sample count next to the rate it describes, so a directional accuracy is never readable without the number of points behind it. It exists because this project once reported 'directional accuracy 100.0%' off five points.
